title: query-level access fence for analytics endpoints and telemetry-aware enforcement
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a query-level access fence for analytics endpoints that enforces tenant and entitlement constraints early in the request path. The fence will operate at the analytics API gateway and at the dataplane query layer to provide end-to-end protection for usage views (console dashboards, exports, ad-hoc queries). Goals: prevent unauthorized cross-tenant visibility, minimize token-level performance impact, make enforcement auditable, and allow progressive rollout with opt-in telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: All analytics query endpoints mechanically add tenant + entitlement predicates before execution when caller requires scoping
A lightweight middleware exists at the gateway that short-circuits unauthorized requests with 403 and logs audit context
Query rewrites are deterministic and do not change aggregation semantics for scoped queries
End-to-end traces include the access decision id and cause for every denied or masked response
Performance regression on p95 latency for typical queries is < 15% compared to baseline
Canary rollout configured (10% / 50% / 100%) with rollback hooks tied to error and latency thresholds
tasks: Design: formalize query predicate model (attributes, entitlements, temporal scopes)
Implement gateway middleware to evaluate entitlements and attach access token claim context
Implement query rewriter module for the dataplane that injects tenant-aware predicates
Add audit event emitter with structured fields (request_id, decision_id, principal, reason)
Create feature-flag + rollout config for progressive enablement
End-to-end testing: unit tests, integration tests, and load test harness with production-like dataset
Docs: update Console API docs and internal runbook for troubleshooting denied queries
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal only (dev + staging) for 2 weeks to validate correctness. Phase 2: canary 10% of production traffic for 3 days, monitor errors and p95 latency. Phase 3: expand to 50% for 48 hours, then full rollout. Rollback triggers: >1.5x increase in 5xxs or >20% p95 latency regression or any data-leak incident. Post-rollout: runback audit and confirm no masked rows for entitled users.
notes: Trade-off: two-layer enforcement (gateway + dataplane) adds complexity but minimizes blast radius for middleware failures
We considered a pure row-level policy engine, but query rewrite is faster and simpler to integrate with legacy aggregation pipelines
Caching: entitlement results should be cached short-lived (30s) and invalidated on role changes; cache size bounded per-region
Telemetry: include decision_id in logs and traces so we can correlate audit events with cost/latency anomalies
Security review required because this changes visibility; flagged for early SRE and security design review
communication: Slack: #console-engineering: announced design 2026-02-12 and asked for feedback
RFC: internal RFC link (drive) added to PR for security review
Customer notice: n/a (no end-user visible API change expected)
post_mortem_plan: If any data exposure or mis-scoping is detected during or after rollout, run immediate frozen rollout, capture the last-good queries from audit log, notify affected teams, open an incident in PagerDuty, and produce a formal post-mortem with action items and owner assignments within 72 hours.
